title: Preservation Across an Oddness Test
statement: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register machine with oracle, input $x$, and configuration guard $G$. Suppose the instruction at live state $l$ tests whether register $r$ is odd, continuing at $l_1$ if its remainder modulo $2$ is $1$ and at $l_0$ otherwise. If the configuration with state $l$, valuation $v$, and no answer satisfies $G$, the remainder of $v(r)$ modulo $2$ is not $1$, and the configuration at state $l_0$ with valuation $v$ and no answer is terminating under $G$ and accepts exactly when proposition $P$ holds, then the original configuration has those same properties.
hypotheses_covered: The instruction at state l tests whether register r has remainder 1 modulo 2, with branches l1 and l0
The remainder of v(r) modulo 2 is not 1
The l0 successor is terminating under G and accepts exactly when P holds
